[0] Water damage is one of those "spend a little on a sensor now to save a fortune in repairs later" problems, whether it's the floor or the cabinetry. Leak sensors have always been one of the best-value products in the smart home, and Shelly's new Flood S Gen4 makes getting started easier than ever. Priced under $30, Matter-certified, and working with Apple Home right out of the box.

[1] HomeKit Weekly is a column dedicated to smart home accessories, automation tips, and everything related to Apple's smart home framework.

[2] A larger sensing surface

[3] Most leak sensors on the market rely on small metal probes on the underside, meaning water has to pool in exactly the right spot to trigger them. Shelly's new sensor takes a different approach, featuring three large stainless-steel sensing pads across the bottom of the device. The contact area is significantly bigger, which means water can be detected faster and in more locations — exactly why you'd put one of these under a water heater or a washing machine.

[4] These pads are also sensitive enough to pick up clean or low-conductivity water, such as condensation dripping from an air-conditioner. These kinds of leaks are usually harder to notice. The Flood S Gen4's body is slim enough to slide under appliances, behind toilets, and beneath sinks — precisely where you'd most want to place a device like this.

[5] Matter / Apple Home support

[6] The Flood S Gen4 is Matter-certified, supports both Wi-Fi and Zigbee, and works with Apple Home, Google Home, Amazon Alexa, SmartThings, and Home Assistant. Once you've added it to Apple Home, the automation possibilities expand significantly:

  • [7] The instant water is detected, cut power to the washing machine or dishwasher (if plugged into a smart plug)
  • [8] Trigger all the smart bulbs in the house
  • [9] Receive a clear, no-nonsense leak alert on your iPhone (especially useful when you're not at home)

[10] Modes, alerts, and battery life

[11] The device has a built-in local alert, so as well as the notification on your phone, the people in the house will hear it even from another room. Shelly offers two operating modes — flood detection and rain detection — and three alert settings (strong, normal, eco), letting you strike a balance between leak-detection speed and battery life. The included CR123A battery lasts up to two years.

[12] The bottom line

[13] At under $30, this is the sort of accessory you'll buy three or four of without thinking twice. One in front of the water heater, one in front of the dishwasher, one under the washing machine, one under the kitchen sink. With Matter and Apple Home support, you get alerts in the Home app and can build Apple Home automations around it. There's a lot to like here, and I can't find anything not to like. Trust me, buying a flood sensor is one of the smartest investments you can make in your smart home.

[14] You can buy the Shelly Flood S Gen4 directly from Amazon or the Shelly website.
